chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Ahmad ibn al-Mithammi, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about selling thread for garments that are spread out (unsewn), where the thread is more than the measure of the garments. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell thread for unsewn garments if the thread quantity exceeds the garment size?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of thread for garments while the fabric is still spread out, even if the thread's quantity exceeds the final volume of the clothes. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of permissibility in conditional sales where the excess material serves as a necessary buffer or margin for the manufacturing process, distinguishing it from *gharar* (uncertainty). The hadith underscores the practical flexibility in commercial transactions, allowing for reasonable variances in material quantity to ensure the viability of the trade.
